Rmarkdown documents can be sourced and executed in sequence, similar to a `main.R` R script. Each called-on document is called a "child" (and instead of `main.R`, the typical name for the 'main' RMarkdown is `index.Rmd`).

The easiest way to include one RMarkdown inside another is to call the "child" in the header option of a new code chunk. The entire code chunk looks like:

`{r, child=c('Rmarkdown-intro.Rmd')}`

See more examples and detail here: 

- <https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/child-document.html>

To take this to the next level, check out the `bookdown` package . This is specifically built to

-   Make it easier to handle and join multiple RMarkdown documents

-   Add functionality for handling figures and equations, such as automatic numbering and cross-referencing

As the author says [@xie2024]:

> Despite the package name containing the word "book", bookdown is not only for books. The "book" can be anything that consists of multiple R Markdown documents meant to be read in a linear sequence, such as course handouts, study notes, a software manual, a thesis, or even a diary. In fact, many bookdown features apply to single R Markdown documents as well.

# Example 

This document is an example of calling one Rmarkdown document, the workshop tutorial, from within another. Note that the references in each Rmarkdown are collated neatly at the end in a single bibliography. See the Rmarkdown bible for more info [@yihuixie2023].

## Tutorial: Intro to Rmarkdown

```{r, child=c('Rmarkdown-intro.Rmd')}
```
